chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the testimony of the blind man, so he said, 'Yes, if he is established (as valid/competent).'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a blind person valid in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the validity of a blind person's testimony is affirmed, contingent upon their being 'established' (ithbat), a term scholars interpret as either possessing sufficient sensory perception to verify facts or having a reliable witness confirm their identity and competence. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that physical disability does not inherently invalidate legal capacity (ahliyyah) if the essential faculties for truthfulness and observation remain intact. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic evidence law in accommodating diverse conditions while maintaining judicial integrity.
